Honorable Commissioners,

{ write to you today not merely as a concerned citizen of this great state, but as someone
whose blood runs deep with the foundational engineering and industrial history that built
modern American energy supremacy. | urge you in the strongest possible terms to throw
your full support behind House Bill 5066. Furthermore, | implore this Commission to
decisively reject any attempts at delay, deferral, or judicial grandstanding—most
specifically the cynical, politicatly motivated amicus brief filed by Attorney General Ken
Paxton.

If my late grandfather, Arthur R. Mardoian, were alive today, he would fiercely support this
bill. He spent his life defending the integrity of American industry and traveled to
Washington, D.C., time and again to advocate for smart, forward-thinking policy that
ensured our country could reach its true industrial and economic potential. He knew what
it took to build this nation, and he would have zero patience for regulatory obstructionism
disguised as legal posturing.

Let us call Attorney General Paxton’s brief what it is: a transparent, destructive political
stunt that does nothing to protect Texans, but everything to advance partisan theater. Itis
astounding that Mr. Paxton can readily find the time to wreak havoc across our oiland
energy sectors for political headlines yet sits idly by while the progressive governor of
Pennsylvania actively violates Texan sovereignty and undermines our great law
enforcement. Mr, Paxton’s interference is not just an embarrassment; it is a direct threat to
the economic engine of our republic. It will ultimately hurt the energy sector of our great

 state and severely stunt the growth and operational momentum of the Permian Basin—the
very heart of American energy independence.

True innovation requires vision, courage, and an unyielding commitment to progress and
persistence—qualities that appear entirely foreign to those attempting to derail HB 5066
from the sidelines, like Attorney General Paxton. My grandfather, Arthur R. Mardoian,
understood the inner workings of industrial progress intimately. During his distinguished
career with Mobil Oil, he authored the company-wide Transportation Emergency Response
System (TERS) and led the task force that successfully operated the world's first
commercial zeolitic catalyst plant. His life’s work contributed fundamentally to industrial
safety, environmental protection, and advanced refining chemistry.

While those contributions were implemented nationwide and globally by Mobil—now
ExxonMobil—they directly fortified major energy hubs like Texas in two vital ways:

¢ Rapid Environmental Spill Containment: My Grandfather’s TERS framework was
engineered to react within minutes to hydrocarbon and hazardous material spills across
the United States. Given Texas's massive concentration of refineries, pipelines, and
transport terminals, particularly along the Gulf Coast and major logistics corridors, his
systematic emergency protocols provided facility operators and transit teams with the
tools needed to contain environmental leaks rapidly, safeguarding local ecosystems and
water tables.

¢ Advanced Refining and Chemical Efficiency: As the leader of the task force that
pioneered high-performance zeolite catalysts, including the foundational work behind the
MCM-22 family, my grandfather revolutionized large-scale hydrocarbon processing. These
innovations enabled cleaner, higher-purity chemical and fuel production with significantly
lower energy footprints—technology that remains foundational to massive Texas refining
complexes, such as ExxonMobit's Beaumont facility, to optimize both output and safety.

My Grandfather knew how to innovate when he saw it, and he knew how to recognize a
bureaucratic or political parasite when it stood in the path of progress and justice. He
championed systems built on constitutional principles, structural integrity, and the rule of
law—echoing the enduring wisdom of our founding fathers, who understood that true
liberty requires economic sovereignty free from arbitrary, politically driven interference.

 House Bill 5066 preserves the framework necessary to keep our grid stable, our markets
competitive, and our industries thriving. Do not let outside political posturing derail the
future of Texas. Reject the amicus brief, refuse any calls for deferral, and pass House Bill
5066 immediately.

Sincerely,
Richard T. Mardoian
